kv_cache.What is a KV cache, and why does it spee: Each decode step would recompute K and V for all previous tokens. Caching them makes each new step cost O(context).
kv_cache.What does it cost in memory?: 2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * seq_len * batch * bytes per element.
kv_cache.How do you append new keys and values ea: Compute K and V for the new token and concatenate along the sequence dimension, or write into a preallocated buffer.
kv_cache.How do you handle the causal mask during: Prefill needs the full causal mask. A single decode token can attend to everything cached, so no mask is needed.
kv_cache.Compute KV cache size for a given model: Plug numbers into 2 * L * n_kv * d_head * S * bytes: for example LLaMA-2 7B at 4k tokens in fp16 is about 2 GB per sequence.
kv_cache.How do MQA, GQA and MLA reduce KV cache: MQA and GQA reduce the number of KV heads. MLA caches a small latent vector and reconstructs K and V.
kv_cache.Why does batch size at inference get lim: GPU memory minus weights, divided by per-sequence KV size, caps the batch.

int8_quantization.What is weight quantization, and why INT: Store weights in 8 bits with a scale to cut memory and bandwidth by about 4x versus fp32 (2x versus fp16).
int8_quantization.Why per-channel scales rather than per-t: Different output channels have different ranges. One scale for all wastes precision on small channels.
int8_quantization.How do you compute the scale and round t: scale = max(|w|) / 127 per row; q = round(w / scale), then clamp to [-128, 127] as this exercise says. With that scale the values already land in [-127, 127].
int8_quantization.Symmetric versus asymmetric quantization: Symmetric uses zero point 0 and suits zero-centered weights. Asymmetric adds a zero point for skewed ranges such as post-ReLU activations.
int8_quantization.How do you dequantize in the forward pas: Compute w approximately as q * scale, then run the matmul, or fold the scale into the output.
int8_quantization.Why are outliers a problem for INT8 in L: A few activation channels are huge, so one scale crushes the rest. LLM.int8 keeps outliers in fp16; SmoothQuant moves scale from activations to weights.
int8_quantization.Weight-only versus weight-and-activation: Weight-only saves memory and helps memory-bound decoding. W8A8 also speeds up compute but must handle activation outliers.

topk_sampling.What are top-k and top-p sampling?: Top-k keeps the k most likely tokens; top-p keeps the smallest set whose probabilities add up to p. Both renormalize and sample.
topk_sampling.What does temperature do before filterin: Dividing logits by T sharpens (T < 1) or flattens (T > 1) the distribution, which changes which tokens pass a top-p cutoff.
topk_sampling.How do you implement top-p with a sorted: Sort probabilities descending, take the cumsum, mask tokens whose cumsum before them already exceeds p, then scatter the mask back.
topk_sampling.How do you make sure at least one token: Always keep the top token, for example by shifting the mask one position right or forcing index 0 to stay.
topk_sampling.In which order do temperature, top-k and: Usually temperature first, then top-k, then top-p. Say what changes if top-p runs on untempered probabilities.
topk_sampling.Top-p versus min-p versus typical sampli: Top-p uses a fixed probability mass. Min-p keeps tokens above a fraction of the top probability, adapting to confidence. Typical sampling targets expected information content.
topk_sampling.How do sampling settings affect RL rollo: Rollouts need diversity for exploration, and the training logprobs must match the sampling distribution. Evaluation often uses greedy or fixed settings with pass@k.

logits_processors.What do temperature, top-k and top-p eac: Temperature rescales all logits; top-k keeps a fixed count; top-p keeps the smallest set covering p of the mass.
logits_processors.Why does the repetition penalty divide p: The goal is always to make the token less likely. Dividing a negative logit would make it larger, so negatives are multiplied instead.
logits_processors.Walk through implementing top-p on a bat: Sort descending and take the cumulative sum. Remove a token when the sum of the tokens before it already reaches p, so the token that crosses the threshold stays. Scatter the mask back with the sort indices.
logits_processors.Why does the order of temperature and to: Temperature changes the shape before the cutoff. Example: logits [2, 1, 0] with p = 0.8 keep a different number of tokens at T = 0.5 than at T = 2.
logits_processors.How should top-k treat ties, and what do: Ties at the k-th value: either keep all tied tokens or break by index. torch.topk makes no stable guarantee, so the spec must say.
logits_processors.Top-p versus top-k versus min-p for crea: Creative writing wants moderate p or min-p for diversity. Code wants low temperature or a small k because one wrong token breaks it.
logits_processors.Repetition penalty versus frequency and: Repetition penalty scales logits of any seen token once. Frequency penalty grows with count; presence penalty is a flat one-time subtraction. They can suppress needed repeats such as names or code.

beam_search.What is beam search, and how does it dif: Keep the B best partial sequences by total log-probability at each step, instead of only the single best token as greedy does.
beam_search.Why is beam search common in translation: Translation has one mostly-correct answer where likelihood tracks quality. Chat wants diverse, natural text, and beams give bland, repetitive output.
beam_search.How do you expand and prune beams at eac: Expand each beam by all tokens, score cumulative log-prob, keep the top B overall. Store tokens, score and finished flag per beam.
beam_search.How do you handle beams that finish with: Move finished beams to a completed list and keep searching with the rest until enough finish or max length is reached.
beam_search.Why use log-probabilities, and what is l: Summing logs avoids underflow from multiplying probabilities. Longer sequences accumulate more negative log-probs, so normalizing avoids preferring short outputs.
beam_search.Beam search versus sampling: quality, di: Beam finds higher-likelihood text, but high likelihood is often dull and repetitive. Sampling is more diverse but noisier.
beam_search.How does beam width affect compute and o: Compute grows linearly with width. Wider beams find higher-likelihood outputs that can be worse (the beam search curse), such as empty or short translations.

speculative_decoding.What is speculative decoding, and why do: A cheap draft proposes several tokens and the big model verifies them in one forward pass, turning serial decode steps into one parallel step.
speculative_decoding.Why is the output distribution unchanged: The accept-reject rule with residual resampling is a form of rejection sampling that reproduces the target distribution exactly.
speculative_decoding.Walk through the accept rule min(1, p ov: Accept a draft token x with probability min(1, p(x) / q(x)). If the target likes it at least as much, always accept.
speculative_decoding.How do you sample the correction token o: Sample from the normalized max(0, p - q), the probability mass the draft underweighted.
speculative_decoding.What happens when all draft tokens are a: You get one bonus token sampled from the target at the next position, since its distribution was already computed.
speculative_decoding.What determines the speedup, and when do: The acceptance rate and the draft's cost relative to the target. It vanishes with a poorly matched draft or a compute-bound large batch.
speculative_decoding.Draft model versus self-speculation meth: A separate draft needs a matching tokenizer and its own memory. Medusa and EAGLE add heads on the target model, avoiding a second model but needing training.

tensor_parallel.What is tensor parallelism in Megatron-s: Split each weight matrix across GPUs so every GPU computes part of every layer, which cuts per-GPU memory and compute.
tensor_parallel.Why column-parallel first and row-parall: Column-split the first matrix so each GPU holds complete hidden units and can apply the nonlinearity locally. Row-split the second so partial outputs just need summing.
tensor_parallel.Where do the all-reduce operations happe: Forward: one all-reduce after the row-parallel layer. Backward: one all-reduce of the input gradient before the column-parallel layer.
tensor_parallel.Why no communication between the two lin: Each GPU's slice of hidden units feeds directly into its matching rows of the second matrix. Nothing needs to be exchanged.
tensor_parallel.How do you split biases correctly?: The first layer's bias is split with its columns. The second layer's bias is added once after the all-reduce, not on every rank.
tensor_parallel.Why is tensor parallelism usually kept w: It needs an all-reduce in every layer, which demands NVLink bandwidth. Crossing nodes over the network is too slow.
tensor_parallel.Tensor versus pipeline versus data paral: TP within a node, pipeline across nodes for depth, data parallel on the outside. Mention 3D parallelism and the memory and bandwidth each needs.

fsdp_step.What is FSDP, and how does it differ fro: It shards parameters, gradients and optimizer state across data-parallel workers instead of replicating them, and gathers parameters only when needed.
fsdp_step.What does ZeRO stage 3 shard?: All three: parameters, gradients and optimizer states.
fsdp_step.Walk through all-gather before forward a: Before a layer runs, all-gather its full parameters, then free them. After backward, reduce-scatter the gradients so each worker keeps the sum for its shard.
fsdp_step.Why is the gradient divided by the numbe: It averages the per-worker gradients so the result equals the gradient of the global mean loss.
fsdp_step.How does each worker update only its sha: Each worker runs the optimizer only on the parameter slice and optimizer state it owns.
fsdp_step.What does FSDP cost in communication com: About 1.5x DDP's communication volume (all-gather forward and backward plus reduce-scatter), in exchange for much less memory.
fsdp_step.FSDP versus tensor parallelism versus pi: FSDP when memory is the problem and the interconnect is good. TP for huge layers within a node. PP for very deep models across slow links.

ring_attention.What is ring attention, and why is it ne: It splits a long sequence across devices and passes K and V blocks around a ring, so no device holds the full attention.
ring_attention.How does it parallelize across the seque: Each device owns a chunk of queries and computes attention against every K/V block as the blocks rotate past.
ring_attention.How do K and V chunks rotate around the: At each step, send your current K/V block to the next device and receive one from the previous. After N steps every device has seen all blocks.
ring_attention.How does online softmax combine partial: Keep a running max, sum and output per query and rescale as each block arrives, as in FlashAttention.
ring_attention.How do you handle causal masking across: Blocks entirely in the future are skipped, the diagonal block gets a triangular mask, and past blocks need no mask. Note the load imbalance.
ring_attention.How does communication overlap with comp: Send the next block while computing on the current one. It hides communication when block compute takes longer than the transfer.
ring_attention.Ring attention versus other sequence par: Ulysses uses all-to-all to switch from sequence sharding to head sharding. Its communication is lower, but parallelism is capped by the number of heads.
